findings.title: Override days skip busy checks and can double-book
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once any date override falls on the same calendar day as the slot, dateOverrideExist is set and the function returns true as soon as the slot is not rejected as outside that override. That return happens before the busy-interval loop. Fixed hosts and round-robin hosts therefore look free for every slot inside an override window even when they already have a Cal booking or calendar conflict covering that time, so the booking page will offer times that cannot actually be taken.

findings.title: All-day blocked overrides never match
findings.body: A zero-length date override (start equal to end) is the usual way an organizer marks a day unavailable. The check compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and is always false, so that branch never runs. Combined with the early return when dateOverrideExist is set, a blocked day is treated as fully available instead of closed, and busy times on that day are also skipped.

findings.title: Working-hours filter rejects valid fixed-host slots
findings.body: The new working-hours gate uses slot start minutes for both start and end, so a slot that begins inside hours but runs past endTime is not detected. It also uses Array.find and treats the first same-day range that does not contain the slot as 'outside hours'. A host with two ranges on one day (for example 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) will fail the check for almost every slot, because each slot misses at least one range. Those slots are then removed for every fixed host, which can make an otherwise bookable round-robin event show no availability. Days with no working-hour entry are not rejected at all, so a fixed host can still be offered on days they do not work.

findings.title: Override date match mixes server-local and UTC formatting
findings.body: slotStartTime is a UTC dayjs, but the override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format(...), which formats in the server's local timezone, not UTC or the organizer zone. The offset itself is also applied to an absolute instant and then compared with UTC slot instants. On any host whose TZ is not UTC, or when the organizer offset moves the override across midnight, the same-day test and the isBefore/isAfter window checks attach the override to the wrong day or the wrong clock times, so fixed-host overrides still do not constrain the slots the PR is trying to fix.

findings.title: Timezone-adjusted overrides lose the day when they cross midnight
findings.body: Override start and end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced to hour() and minute() only. If the shift crosses midnight, hour() wraps to the other side of the day (for example 01:00 minus a 10h offset becomes 15:00) and the previous/next day is discarded. buildSlots then places that window on the invitee's current day. Attendees in a timezone far from the organizer see the override on the wrong date, or miss it, which is the timezone bug this change is meant to fix whenever the adjusted range is not on the same calendar day.

findings.title: New test does not cover either bug the PR claims to fix
findings.body: The only added assertion re-requests the same personal-event override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the identical UTC slot list. It never builds a round-robin event with a fixed host, never asserts that slots outside the fixed host's override disappear, and never checks that an override moves to a different invitee-local calendar day. A regression in checkIfIsAvailable or in the midnight-crossing offset math would still pass CI.
